inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income ($0.12m) is immaterial and NOT stripped -- CHI is a NET DEBT company (net debt $331.8m, ~3.6x EBITDA), not net cash, so the double-count risk this adjustment guards against does not apply here.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K equivalent: CHI.NZ FY2025 Annual Report, Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity (line 'Equity-settled share-based payments' $272k) and Note 18 Share-based payments ($0.1m ESS + $0.1m LTI Share Rights + $0.1m CEO Initial Share Rights = ~$0.3m). SBC is genuinely negligible (0.19% of revenue) for this asset-heavy infrastructure business -- verified against Note 18, not backfilled from an ambiguous reconciliation line.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: STRUCTURAL BREAK, not a normal divergence: Channel closed its Marsden Point oil refinery in April 2022 and converted to a fuel import terminal, making FY2018-FY2021 data describe a DEAD business (revenue fell from $359m to $140m BY DESIGN as refining margin risk was shed for high-margin contracted infrastructure income). Full-history CAGRs (revenue, EPS, equity) spanning this break are MEANINGLESS and are deliberately left null above. Only FY2023-FY2025 describe the current business, giving just 2 years of clean post-conversion data -- too short for a reliable CAGR. The FY23-25 equity CAGR (24.97%) is NOT used: it is an artifact of a $381m non-cash asset revaluation plus a $50m equity raise in FY2024, not earnings retention (retained earnings are deeply NEGATIVE, -$319.6m at FY2025). The selected growth driver (4.5%, the weighted average of the Year 1-10 base-case revenue growth path) instead reflects: (1) already-CONTRACTED fee step-ups from four new storage contracts signed 2024-2025 (~$170m of incremental revenue over 15yrs), the Government strategic diesel reserve (~$14.4m/yr to end-2027), and the Somerton Melbourne pipeline stake (accretive from FY2026), phasing in through FY2026-2028; decelerating to (2) the long-run PPI/CPI contractual fee escalation (~2.2-2.5%) embedded in the Terminal Services Agreements once new contracts are fully phased in. This is a bottom-up contracted-revenue build, not a historical trend extrapolation.

wacc_rationale.beta_adjustment: Below-market beta (~0.6-0.7) appropriate for take-or-pay contracted infrastructure cashflow, largely offsetting a chunk of the standard NZ small/mid-cap ERP -- netted into the components below rather than shown as a separate multiplier

premiums_added.customer_concentration: +1.0% -- bp, Mobil and Z Energy are effectively 100% of contracted terminal revenue; loss or distress of any one counterparty is material despite investment-grade quality and shareholder alignment
premiums_added.structural_demand_decline_ev_decarbonisa: +1.0% -- long-run light-vehicle EV adoption and eventual aviation decarbonisation structurally erode liquid fuel throughput; fixed take-or-pay fees cushion but do not eliminate this
premiums_added.contract_renewal_cliff_2032: +0.5% -- Terminal Services Agreements run to 2032; renewal terms/pricing beyond that date are unknown and sit outside the explicit 10-year forecast window but colour the terminal growth assumption
premiums_added.leverage: +0.5% -- net debt ~3.6x EBITDA (within the company's own 3.0-4.5x shadow BBB/BBB+ target, but materially levered vs an unlevered infra comparator), raising equity cash-flow volatility
premiums_added.small_cap_illiquidity_partial_offset: 0.0% -- NZX/ASX dual-listed with ~NZ$1.4bn market cap and rising international (ASX) shareholder base; no separate illiquidity premium applied given increasing float and institutional ownership

wacc_rationale.contracted_cashflow_discount: -1.5% -- offsetting reduction versus a generic 11-12% NZ small-cap WACC, reflecting genuinely high cash-flow visibility: ~93% of revenue is fixed/take-or-pay and PPI-indexed under signed 10-year contracts with credit-quality counterparties, closer to regulated-utility risk than a discretionary industrial/cyclical business
wacc_rationale.note: 9.0% sits below a typical NZX small-cap WACC (11-12%) because the take-or-pay, PPI-linked contract structure genuinely lowers cash-flow risk versus a cyclical or discretionary business, but ABOVE a regulated-utility WACC (~6-7%) because CHI is not price-regulated, carries real counterparty concentration, and faces a 2032 contract-renewal cliff and long-run decarbonisation risk that a true regulated network does not.

bull.narrative: Marsden Point Energy Precinct progresses faster than base case: Biorefinery consortium reaches FID in 2026 with Channel capturing land/infrastructure lease economics, Special Planning Zone designation accelerates consenting, government fuel-security policy drives further strategic storage demand beyond the current 2027 contract, and the Somerton Melbourne step-out is the first of several accretive Australian bolt-ons. EBITDA margin expands toward ~71-72% on operating leverage over the fixed cost base.

bear.narrative: EV penetration in the NZ light fleet accelerates faster than the Envisory forecast, petrol/diesel throughput volumes decline materially, and Marsden Point Energy Precinct projects (biorefinery, diesel peaker) stall on financing/consenting/policy delay (LNG import facility decision keeps the peaker paused indefinitely). Government diesel reserve contract is not renewed past 2027 amid political scrutiny of the sole-source arrangement. Rising D&A from the FY2024 revaluation compresses margins as fixed costs are spread over a shrinking-to-flat revenue base; leverage headroom tightens.

base.exit_multiple_vs_current_note: Implied exit multiple (14.6x FCF) is BELOW the current market multiple (25.4x owner FCF, 18.4x EV/EBITDA), i.e. the model does NOT assume multiple expansion -- it assumes contraction toward a level more typical of the FY2023-2025 traded range (avg EV/EBITDA 12.3x) as the market's current growth-optionality premium (Marsden Point precinct/biorefinery) normalises once those projects are either delivered or fail to materialise within the 10-year window.

base.note: Entry price sits well below intrinsic value (54% of base IV) because the 15% IRR hurdle far exceeds the 9.0% WACC used to discount a low-growth (~4.5% avg), high cash-flow-visibility infrastructure asset -- this is the expected sanity property (entry << IV when growth << hurdle rate), not a modelling error.
base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

sensitivity.note: Rows at lower WACC are flattened across terminal-growth columns because the 16x-FCF terminal cap binds (not Gordon growth) at those WACC levels -- this is intentional and prevents the model from capitalizing an implausible aggressive exit multiple when the WACC-to-terminal-growth spread narrows.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.basis: FY2023-FY2025 only (post-refinery-conversion years; FY2018-FY2022 excluded as a structurally different, dead refining business)
historical_averages_ex_outliers.pe_note: P/E excluded from the historical comparison set entirely (not just flagged) because reported net income is dominated by non-operating noise unrelated to the contracted terminal business: a $9.1m FY2025 / $12.1m FY2024 discontinued-operations loss (residual refinery conversion costs, disposals, asset revaluations) sits on top of continuing-ops net income that is itself mechanically depressed by the $381m FY2024 non-cash asset revaluation nearly doubling D&A ($38.7m to $45.1m). Continuing-ops P/E alone is 27.5x (FY2024) rising to 57.3x (FY2025) purely from the D&A step-up, not from any earnings deterioration in the underlying cash business -- EV/EBITDA and EV/owner-FCF are the reliable multiples for this ticker.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied P/B (1.07x) sits BELOW both the FY23-25 average (1.17x) and max (1.54x); implied EV/EBITDA (12.51x) sits BELOW the FY23-25 average (12.29x is essentially matched, and well below the 1.5x-max trigger of 24.6x) and far below the current market multiple (18.41x). Base-case upside is negative (-39.7%), so the 'upside>100% in upper-half-of-range' trigger is structurally inapplicable. The base case is, if anything, MORE conservative than the market's own recent trading multiples, not less -- consistent with the deliberate choice to exclude the Marsden Point Energy Precinct/biorefinery optionality (still consortium/FID-dependent, not yet contracted) from the explicit 10-year forecast.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- model passed without adjustment. The wide gap between base-case IV ($2.04) and the current price ($3.38) is NOT attributed to a modelling defect; it reflects the market pricing real growth optionality (biorefinery FID due 2026, Special Planning Zone, further government fuel-security demand) that this DCF deliberately treats as an unmodelled free call option per the conservative infrastructure-annuity framing, rather than assuming its success. See `valuation_philosophy` for the full reasoning.
sanity_check.direction_of_conclusion: The DCF finds CHI.NZ EXPENSIVE relative to a conservative, contracted-cashflow-only base case (-39.7% to base IV), while the BULL case (which assumes meaningful precinct/biorefinery progress) still shows only modest upside (+7.0%) at $3.62. This suggests the current $3.38 price already embeds substantial credit for growth optionality succeeding -- consistent with the stock's +53% run over the past year and a 'Hold' consensus analyst rating with price targets (NZ$2.60-3.00) clustered BELOW the current price cited in the qualitative analysis.

valuation_philosophy.framing: Channel Infrastructure is valued as a REGULATED-LIKE INFRASTRUCTURE / YIELD ASSET, not a growth compounder. This is a natural-monopoly fuel import terminal (sole deep-water jetties + sole pipeline to Auckland) earning largely fixed, take-or-pay, PPI-indexed fees from three investment-grade fuel majors under 10-year Terminal Services Agreements to 2032. The correct valuation lens is closer to a toll-road or airport-runway concession than to a discretionary industrial or consumer growth business.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_equity_cagr: Shareholders' equity CAGR -- the standard 'most conservative' driver for other tickers in this project -- is explicitly REJECTED here. FY2024 equity jumped $499m to $818m almost entirely from a $381m non-cash independent asset revaluation (the terminal infrastructure being revalued upward following the 2022 refinery-to-terminal conversion) plus a $50m equity raise, not from retained earnings (retained earnings remain deeply NEGATIVE at -$319.6m FY2025). Using this as a growth driver would import a one-off accounting revaluation into a perpetuity growth assumption -- a much larger version of the SEK.NZ-style error this project's playbook exists to catch.
valuation_philosophy.why_structural_break_excludes_pre_2022_h: Refining NZ closed its oil refinery in April 2022 and converted the site to a fuel import terminal. FY2018-FY2021 revenue ($359m to $140m by FY2025) reflects a fundamentally different business (crude refining, exposed to refining margin/commodity risk) than the current contracted-infrastructure model. Any CAGR spanning this break (revenue, EPS, or equity) describes the transition from one business to another, not organic growth of the current business, and is therefore left null in `historical_growth` with only the FY2023-2025 post-conversion figures (and a bottom-up contracted-revenue build) used as the growth driver.
valuation_philosophy.growth_driver_construction: The 10-year explicit forecast (rather than the default 5-year) is used because the business is still phasing in already-signed growth contracts (Z Energy jet tank Q3 2026, Higgins/Vinci bitumen terminal Q4 2026, government diesel reserve to end-2027, additional storage extension from Q1 2028, Somerton Melbourne pipeline from FY2026) through FY2028-2029 before settling into a mature, PPI/CPI-indexed growth rate of ~2.2-2.5% by Year 9-10. A 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature, still-elevated growth rate in perpetuity and overstate terminal value. The Marsden Point Energy Precinct redevelopment and Biorefinery consortium (FID expected 2026, PwC-estimated ~$3.3bn GDP impact) are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from all three scenarios' explicit cash flows as unmodelled optionality -- they depend on third-party consortium investment decisions and government policy outside Channel's control, and including them would require speculating on financing structure, ownership share and timing that the company itself has not yet disclosed.
valuation_philosophy.why_ebitda_component_build_not_flat_marg: FY2025 EBITDA margin (66.4%) reflects a business still absorbing one-off costs (ASX dual-listing ~$1m, Somerton acquisition costs ~$1.5m) alongside the tail-end Wiri lease effects (expired Feb 2025). The component build ramps margin modestly to ~68.8% at maturity as these one-offs roll off and fixed costs are spread over a larger contracted revenue base -- a genuine but bounded operating-leverage story, not an unexplained margin expansion.
valuation_philosophy.why_low_wacc_relative_to_typical_nzx_sma: At 9.0% (base case), WACC sits below the 11-12% baseline this project typically applies to NZX small/mid-caps, net of the wacc_rationale components (see assumptions.base.wacc_rationale): a -1.5% contracted-cashflow discount (take-or-pay, PPI-linked, ~93% fixed fee structure with investment-grade counterparties) more than offsets +3.0% of documented structural premiums (customer concentration, EV/decarbonisation demand risk, 2032 contract cliff, leverage). This is deliberately still meaningfully ABOVE a true regulated-utility WACC (~6-7%) because CHI is not price-regulated by a government body and carries genuine counterparty concentration and terminal-value risk a regulated network does not.
valuation_philosophy.why_terminal_growth_capped_at_2pct: Terminal growth (2.0% base, 1.0% bear, 2.5% bull) is capped below long-run NZ nominal GDP growth (~3-4%) to reflect genuine, multi-decade structural fuel-demand decline risk from light-vehicle EV adoption and eventual aviation decarbonisation. This is a business whose PHYSICAL THROUGHPUT is expected to plateau-to-decline over the very long run even though near-to-medium-term fixed/take-or-pay fee escalation provides a cushion; a terminal growth rate assuming indefinite real volume growth would be inconsistent with the company's own commissioned Envisory demand forecast cited in the qualitative analysis.
valuation_philosophy.why_exit_multiple_cap_below_current_mark: The 16x-owner-FCF terminal cap (base case) is set BELOW the current market multiple the stock trades at (25.4x EV/owner-FCF, 18.4x EV/EBITDA at the $3.38 close), reflecting the same growth-optionality exclusion: the market is pricing some probability of the Marsden Point precinct/biorefinery succeeding, while this DCF's explicit and terminal cash flows contain none of that. The gap between the DCF's conservative multiple and the market's richer one is the honest measure of how much of the current share price is optionality value versus contracted-cashflow value.
valuation_philosophy.sbc_and_leverage_notes: SBC is genuinely negligible for this capital-intensive infrastructure business (~0.19% of revenue, ~$0.27m FY2025 across three small employee/LTI schemes) and is deducted but immaterial to the outcome. The dominant balance-sheet feature is instead leverage: $334.7m total debt against $2.9m cash (net debt ~$331.8m, ~3.6x FY2025 EBITDA), within the company's own 3.0-4.5x shadow BBB/BBB+ target but a real equity-value driver -- net debt is subtracted in full from enterprise value in every scenario, and +0.5% of WACC premium is attributed to leverage risk specifically.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: This DCF answers 'what is Channel Infrastructure worth as a contracted, take-or-pay fuel-terminal annuity, before crediting any Marsden Point precinct optionality?' Base case: NZ$2.04 (-39.7% vs $3.38). Bull case (meaningful precinct/biorefinery progress): NZ$3.62 (+7.0%). The market's current price sits between these, closer to the bull case, implying investors already assign material probability-weighted value to growth projects this model deliberately treats as a free option. Investors who believe Marsden Point Energy Precinct and the biorefinery FID will materialise should weight toward the bull case; investors sceptical of third-party-dependent, policy-contingent mega-projects should treat the ~$2.00-2.20 base/weighted range as the more defensible anchor, with the current price representing a real premium for optionality rather than a margin of safety.
